title: FeNO, Timed Walk Testing & Exercise Oxygen Titration Quiz

questions.text: What happens to FeNO as airway inflammation worsens?

answers.text: It becomes unrelated to airway inflammation

questions.text: FeNO is measured in which unit?
Which is an indication for FeNO testing?

answers.text: Determine likely response to corticosteroid treatment

questions.text: When possible, how long should a patient refrain from eating and drinking before FeNO measurement?
Which pre-test factor can increase FeNO with maximum effect 2 hours after ingestion?
When should FeNO be performed relative to spirometry or other PFTs?

answers.text: Always before spirometry or other PFTs
It does not matter according to the source

questions.text: In adults, which FeNO value indicates eosinophilic inflammation is unlikely?
In symptomatic adult patients, FeNO greater than 50 ppb suggests what?

answers.text: Eosinophilic inflammation and corticosteroid responsiveness are likely

questions.text: What does the timed walk test measure?

answers.text: Distance walked on a flat, hard surface in 6 minutes

questions.text: Which condition is listed as an indication for a single functional-status timed walk measurement?
What is the minimum hallway distance listed for a timed walk test?
Before the timed walk, how long should the patient sit before baseline data are obtained?
During the timed walk, what happens if the patient stops to rest?

answers.text: The test clock stops until the patient restarts
The technician must walk beside the patient

questions.text: If a patient is on supplemental O2 during the timed walk, who should carry the gas source?

answers.text: The technician walking behind the patient
A second staff member pacing the patient
No one; oxygen should always be removed

questions.text: What change in 6-minute walk distance is clinically significant in most disease states?
What is the purpose of oxygen titration with exercise?

answers.text: Determine the degree of desaturation and/or hypoxemia on exertion
Determine exhaled nitric oxide after eating

questions.text: Which is a relative contraindication to oxygen titration with exercise?

answers.text: Invalid pulse oximetry from COHb or decreased perfusion

questions.text: Which is an absolute contraindication to oxygen titration with exercise?

answers.text: SaO2 or SpO2 less than 85% on room air
Resting systolic BP greater than 200 torr

questions.text: When testing a patient on room air, what should be done if SpO2 drops below 85%?

answers.text: Stop the patient and have them recover before continuing
Increase oxygen by 1-2 L without slowing the patient
Ignore the reading until the end of the test

questions.text: When testing a patient on oxygen, what should be done if SpO2 drops below 88%?

answers.text: Increase oxygen 1-2 L at a time to maintain saturation at least 89%
